requirements.title: Instants carry an explicit UTC offset; non-UTC offsets are normalised to UTC
Offset-less ('naive') instants: rejected, or assumed to be UTC
Malformed or non-existent instants/dates are rejected with INVALID_INSTANT / INVALID_DATE
Proleptic Gregorian leap-year rule (4 / 100 / 400)
Weekday naming: ISO number and Sunday-first Islamic names
Days in month
A Waqt day is the half-open interval [Maghrib(D), Maghrib(D+1))
At the exact opening Maghrib the new day has begun (position 00:00:00)
One microsecond before a Maghrib belongs to the previous day; days tile without gap or overlap
The day label (Hijri date, weekday) is that of the civil date on which the CLOSING Maghrib falls
Position is elapsed SI time since the opening Maghrib and is not clamped at 24:00:00
Day length is the real interval, not 86400 s
Civil dates use the location's IANA zone (date line, DST) — not UTC and not solar time
The Waqt day depends only on the instant: all instants inside a day give the same day and events
Event definitions: Fajr/Isha angles, sunrise/Maghrib -0.8333 deg, Dhuhr transit, Asr shadow ratio (accuracy bands in CONFORMANCE 5)
An event's reading is its instant minus the day's opening Maghrib
The closing Maghrib is listed at the day length; Isha is listed beyond the day length
Events after local midnight stay in the day of their transit (never move to the next civil date)
Fajr/Isha angle and Asr ratio change only their own event, never the day boundary
Elevation (dip) shifts sunrise and Maghrib only
waqt.compute next_event: by OCCURRENCE (includes tonight's Isha) or only among the listed events
Polar day/night (no Maghrib): status UNDEFINED with a reason, never a guessed time
An event that does not occur is omitted, never approximated; other events remain defined
Both implementations must agree on WHICH events exist away from the transition latitude
Existence of grazing events within a few arc-minutes of their threshold
arithmetic-tabular conversion Gregorian -> Hijri (epoch JDN 1948440)
arithmetic-tabular leap-year pattern within the 30-year cycle
arithmetic-tabular reverse conversion is exact and round-trips
Non-existent Hijri dates are rejected (INVALID_HIJRI_DATE), never silently normalised
umm-al-qura reproduces the validated New Year dates (1438, 1440, 1441, 1447)
umm-al-qura months have 29 or 30 days and Gregorian<->Hijri round-trips
umm-al-qura month boundaries away from the validated anchors (threshold-sensitive months)
declared / local-observation override applies only on the exact label date; otherwise tabular
Providers without a fixed rule reject reverse conversion (UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION)
Swapping the calendar provider changes only the label, never an instant or position
umm-al-qura supported range and the error returned outside it
Hard remote failures (timeout, network error, 429, 5xx) fall back to local umm-al-qura with the stable reason code
Soft failures (4xx, malformed, date-mismatch, implausible) fall back with the stable reason code
Dates outside 1900-01-01..2076-12-31 and a disabled provider never leave the process
Cache hit within the TTL; stale-if-error up to 7 days, labelled remote-stale
Circuit breaker after a hard failure; Retry-After honoured and capped
The fallback result names the provider that actually produced it
Soft-failure counting and outbound budget details
Point resolution: instant, anchor, event slots, next/prev occurrence, position, offset, fraction
Windows are half-open; unbounded ends; inside/before/after relation
Deadlines: pending / reached / passed with signed remaining seconds
Three undefined statuses; strict vs skip policy; evaluate reports unknown, not false
Span classification: strict-interior Maghrib crossing, civil midnight independent
event_position reports listed and containing positions; next_event/until/since
Derived instants use integer microseconds with half-up rounding
Scheduling over LIVE astronomy agrees with the table-driven result within astronomy tolerance
Calendar rules: month_day, month_end, nth_weekday_of_month
Islamic week: seven consecutive days from a configurable first day
Fiscal year resolves start/end rules; end before start is rejected
Academic year: opening, closing, terms, holidays
Unresolvable rules fail with INVALID_CALENDAR_RULE
Instant representation: UTC and civil Gregorian views of one instant, plus Waqt position
Gregorian date + place -> the Waqt day whose closing Maghrib falls on that date
Boundary crossing: civil midnight and Maghrib independent; strictly-interior rule
Out-of-range latitude/longitude is rejected
Unknown IANA time zone is rejected
Unknown calendar provider is rejected
Non-physical astronomy profile parameters are rejected
